q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of non-woven PP bags per kg?
title: Non-woven bag carbon footprint per kg
short: Multiply the polypropylene granules used per kg of fabric by a resin factor, add spunbond line electricity, printing ink and bag-making electricity, then divide by kilograms of bags sold. Resin is usually most of the total; trim waste sent back as regrind is not new resin.

ul: PP granules: the largest share; use a supplier or database factor per kg.
Printing inks and lamination film for laminated bags.
Spunbond line: extruder, spinneret, quench air and calender heating.

p: Report per kg and give bag weight by size and GSM, so a buyer can convert. Count trim waste recycled in-house once.

example.title: Worked example: non-woven unit per kg (one month)
lines: Plant total: 63,900 / 120,000 = 0.532 kg CO2 per kg
Add PP resin and masterbatch for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
